api_host.description: The API host to connect to (mostly useful for testing).

api_key.description: The API key for authenticating with the Cloudsmith API.

headers.description: Additional HTTP headers to include in API requests

access_private_broadcasts.description: If enabled, this token can be used for private broadcasts.

is_active.description: If enabled, the token will allow downloads based on configured restrictions (if any).

limit_date_range_from.description: The starting date/time the token is allowed to be used from.

limit_date_range_to.description: The ending date/time the token is allowed to be used until.

limit_num_clients.description: The maximum number of unique clients allowed for the token. Please note that since clients are calculated asynchronously (after the download happens), the limit may not be imposed immediately but at a later point.

limit_num_downloads.description: The maximum number of downloads allowed for the token. Please note that since downloads are calculated asynchronously (after the download happens), the limit may not be imposed immediately but at a later point.

limit_package_query.description: The package-based search query to apply to restrict downloads to. This uses the same syntax as the standard search used for repositories, and also supports boolean logic operators such as OR/AND/NOT and parentheses for grouping. This will still allow access to non-package files, such as metadata.

limit_path_query.description: The path-based search query to apply to restrict downloads to. This supports boolean logic operators such as OR/AND/NOT and parentheses for grouping. The path evaluated does not include the domain name, the namespace, the entitlement code used, the package format, etc. and it always starts with a forward slash.

name.description: A descriptive name for the entitlement.

namespace.description: Namespace to which this entitlement belongs.

repository.description: Repository to which this entitlement belongs.

slug_perm.description: The permanent slug identifier for the entitlement.

token.description: The literal value of the token to be created.

enabled.description: Whether the entitlement token is enabled or disabled.

identifier.description: The identifier (slug_perm) of the entitlement token.

namespace.description: Namespace to which this entitlement belongs.

repository.description: Repository to which this entitlement belongs.

allow_unknown_licenses.description: Allow unknown licenses within the policy.

created_at.description: The time the policy was created at.

description.description: The description of the license policy.

name.description: The name of the license policy.

on_violation_quarantine.description: On violation of the license policy, quarantine violating packages.

organization.description: Organization to which this policy belongs.

package_query_string.description: A search / filter string of packages to include in the policy.

updated_at.description: The time the policy last updated at.

claims.description: The claims associated with these provider settings

enabled.description: Whether the provider settings should be used for incoming OIDC requests.

mapping_claim.description: The claim key whose values dynamically map to service accounts (dynamic providers only). Mutually exclusive with service_accounts.

name.description: The name of the provider settings are being configured for

namespace.description: Namespace to which this OIDC config belongs.

provider_url.description: The URL from the provider that serves as the base for the OpenID configuration.

service_accounts.description: The service accounts associated with these provider settings (static providers only). Mutually exclusive with mapping_claim/dynamic_mappings.

claim_value.description: The value of the mapping claim.

service_account.description: Service account slug mapped to the claim value.

block.description: Set of dynamic claim value -> service account mappings (order-insensitive, authoritative). Mutually exclusive with service_accounts.

description.description: Description of the package deny policy.

enabled.description: Is the package deny policy enabled?.

name.description: A descriptive name for the package deny policy.

namespace.description: Namespace to which this package deny policy belongs.

package_query.description: The query to match the packages to be blocked.

block.description: Package deny policies control which packages can be downloaded within their repositories.

enabled.description: If true, the policy is enabled.

is_terminal.description: If true and the policy matches, no further policies are evaluated.

precedence.description: The order in which this policy is evaluated relative to other policies.

read_only.description: Whether the policy is read-only. Read-only policies cannot be updated through this provider.

rego.description: The rego source for the policy logic.

version.description: The version of the rego code.

policy_slug_perm.description: The slug_perm of the policy this action belongs to.

precedence.description: The order in which this action occurs relative to other actions for the same policy.

updated_at.description: The time the action was last updated.

tags.description: The tags to add to matching packages.
The tags to remove from matching packages.

package_state.description: The state to set on matching packages.

block.description: Set the state of matching packages.

broadcast_state.description: The broadcast state of the repository. Controls repository visibility and access level for broadcasts. Valid values include: `Off`, `Private`, `Internal`, `Public`, `Open-Source`. Defaults to `Off`.

cdn_url.description: Base URL from which packages and other artifacts are downloaded.

contextual_auth_realm.description: If checked, missing credentials for this repository where basic authentication is required shall present an enriched value in the 'WWW-Authenticate' header containing the namespace and repository. This can be useful for tooling such as SBT where the authentication realm is used to distinguish and disambiguate credentials.

copy_own.description: If checked, users can copy any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

copy_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to copy packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific copy setting.

cosign_signing_enabled.description: When enabled, all pushed (or pulled from upstream) OCI packages and artifacts will be signed using cosign with the repository's ECDSA key. This generates a distinct cosign signature artifact per artifact.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the repository was created.

default_privilege.description: This defines the default level of privilege that all of your organization members have for this repository. This does not include collaborators, but applies to any member of the org regardless of their own membership role (i.e. it applies to owners, managers and members). Be careful if setting this to admin, because any member will be able to change settings.Valid values include: `Admin`, `Read`, `Write`, `None`.

delete_own.description: If checked, users can delete any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

delete_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to delete packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific delete setting.

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the repository was deleted (repositories are soft deleted temporarily to allow cancelling).

description.description: A description of the repository's purpose/contents.

docker_refresh_tokens_enabled.description: If checked, refresh tokens will be issued in addition to access tokens for Docker authentication. This allows unlimited extension of the lifetime of access tokens.

index_files.description: If checked, files contained in packages will be indexed, which increase the synchronisation time required for packages. Note that it is recommended you keep this enabled unless the synchronisation time is significantly impacted.

is_open_source.description: True if this repository is open source.

is_private.description: True if this repository is private.

is_public.description: True if this repository is public.

manage_entitlements_privilege.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to manage entitlement tokens with private repositories. Management is the ability to create, alter, enable, disable or delete all tokens within a repository. Possible values: Read, Write, Admin.

move_own.description: If checked, users can move any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

move_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to move packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific move setting.

name.description: A descriptive name for the repository.

namespace.description: Namespace to which this repository belongs.

namespace_url.description: API endpoint where data about this namespace can be retrieved.

npm_upstream_tags_take_precedence.description: If checked, npm distribution tags from configured upstreams will take precedence over matching local tags. When both upstream and local repositories have the same tag name (e.g., 'latest'), the upstream tag will be used instead of the local one, even if the local repository has a semantically higher version.

nuget_native_signing_enabled.description: When enabled, all pushed (or pulled from upstream) nuget packages and artifacts will be signed using the repository's X.509 RSA certificate. Additionally, the nuget RepositorySignature index will list all of the repository's signing certificates including the ones from configured upstreams.

proxy_npmjs.description: If checked, Npm packages that are not in the repository when requested by clients will automatically be proxied from the public npmjs.org registry. If there is at least one version for a package, others will not be proxied.

proxy_pypi.description: If checked, Python packages that are not in the repository when requested by clients will automatically be proxied from the public pypi.python.org registry. If there is at least one version for a package, others will not be proxied.

raw_package_index_enabled.description: If checked, HTML and JSON indexes will be generated that list all available raw packages in the repository.

raw_package_index_signatures_enabled.description: If checked, the HTML and JSON indexes will display raw package GPG signatures alongside the index packages.

replace_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to republish packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific republish setting. Please note that the user still requires the privilege to delete packages that will be replaced by the new package; otherwise the republish will fail.

replace_packages_by_default.description: If checked, uploaded packages will overwrite/replace any others with the same attributes (e.g. same version) by default. This only applies if the user has the required privilege for the republishing AND has the required privilege to delete existing packages that they don't own.

repository_type.description: The repository type changes how it is accessed and billed. Private repositories can only be used on paid plans, but are visible only to you or authorised delegates. Public repositories are free to use on all plans and visible to all Cloudsmith users.Valid values include: `Private` or `Public`.

resync_own.description: If checked, users can resync any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

resync_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to resync packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific resync setting.

scan_own.description: If checked, users can scan any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

scan_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to scan packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific scan setting.

self_url.description: API endpoint where data about this repository can be retrieved.

show_setup_all.description: If checked, the Set Me Up help for all formats will always be shown, even if you don't have packages of that type uploaded. Otherwise, help will only be shown for packages that are in the repository. For example, if you have uploaded only NuGet packages, then the Set Me Up help for NuGet packages will be shown only.

slug.description: The slug identifies the repository in URIs.

slug_perm.description: The slug_perm immutably identifies the repository. It will never change once a repository has been created.

storage_region.description: The Cloudsmith region in which package files are stored.Supported regions include: Sydney, Australia (au-sydney),Singapore (sg-singapore), Montreal, Canada (ca-montreal), Frankfurt, Germany (de-frankfurt), Oregon,United States (us-oregon), Ohio, United States (us-ohio), Tokyo, Japan (jp-tokyo), London, United Kingdom (gb-london), Dublin, Ireland (ie-dublin) (default)

strict_npm_validation.description: If checked, npm packages will be validated strictly to ensure the package matches specifcation. You can turn this off if you have packages that are old or otherwise mildly off-spec, but we can't guarantee the packages will work with npm-cli or other tooling correctly. Turn off at your own risk!

tag_pre_releases_as_latest.description: If checked, packages pushed with a pre-release component on that version will be marked with the 'latest' tag. Note that if unchecked, a repository containing ONLY pre-release versions, will have no version marked latest which may cause incompatibility with native tools

use_debian_labels.description: If checked, a 'Label' field will be present in Debian-based repositories. It will contain a string that identifies the entitlement token used to authenticate the repository, in the form of 'source=t-'; or 'source=none' if no token was used. You can use this to help with pinning.

use_default_cargo_upstream.description: If checked, dependencies of uploaded Cargo crates which do not set an explicit value for "registry" will be assumed to be available from crates.io. If unchecked, dependencies with unspecified "registry" values will be assumed to be available in the registry being uploaded to. Uncheck this if you want to ensure that dependencies are only ever installed from Cloudsmith unless explicitly specified as belong to another registry.

use_entitlements_privilege.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to see/use entitlement tokens with private repositories. If a user does not have the permission, they will only be able to download packages using other credentials, such as email/password via basic authentication. Use this if you want to force users to only use their user-based token, which is tied to their access (if removed, they can't use it). Possible values: Read, Write, Admin.

use_noarch_packages.description: If checked, noarch packages (if supported) are enabled in installations/configurations. A noarch package is one that is not tied to specific system architecture (like i686).

use_source_packages.description: If checked, source packages (if supported) are enabled in installations/configurations. A source package is one that contains source code rather than built binaries.

use_vulnerability_scanning.description: If checked, vulnerability scanning will be enabled for all supported packages within this repository.

user_entitlements_enabled.description: If checked, users can use and manage their own user-specific entitlement token for the repository (if private). Otherwise, user-specific entitlements are disabled for all users.

view_statistics.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to view repository statistics, to include entitlement-based usage, if applicable. If a user does not have the permission, they won't be able to view any statistics, either via the UI, API or CLI.Valid values include: `Admin`, `Write`, `Read`.

wait_for_deletion.description: If true, terraform will wait for a repository to be permanently deleted before finishing.

created_at.description: The date and time when the connection was created (RFC 3339).

namespace.description: Organization to which the source Repository belongs.

priority.description: Order in which connected repositories are checked (ascending, starting at 1). Ties are broken by age (oldest first).

repository.description: Source Repository from which to add the connection.

slug_perm.description: The immutable slug identifier of the connection.

target_repository.description: The slug of the target Repository to connect to.

cidr_allow.description: The list of IP Addresses for which to allow access, expressed in CIDR notation.

cidr_deny.description: The list of IP Addresses for which to deny access, expressed in CIDR notation.

country_code_allow.description: The list of countries for which to allow access, expressed in ISO 3166-1 country codes.

country_code_deny.description: The list of countries for which to deny access, expressed in ISO 3166-1 country codes.

namespace.description: Organization to which the Repository belongs.

repository.description: Repository to which these Geo/IP rules belong.

organization.description: Organization to which this repository belongs.

repository.description: Repository to which these privileges belong.

retention_count_limit.description: The maximum number of packages to retain. Must be between 0 and 10000.

retention_days_limit.description: The number of days of packages to retain. Must be between 0 and 180. Defaults to 28 days.

retention_enabled.description: If true, the retention lifecycle rules will be activated for the repository and settings will be updated.

retention_group_by_format.description: If true, retention will apply to packages by package formats rather than across all package formats.

retention_group_by_name.description: If true, retention will apply to groups of packages by name rather than all packages.

retention_group_by_package_type.description: If true, retention will apply to packages by package type rather than across all package types for one or more formats.

retention_package_query_string.description: A package search expression which, if provided, filters the packages to be deleted.

retention_size_limit.description: The maximum total size (in bytes) of packages to retain. Must be between 0 and 21474836480 (21.47 GB / 21474.83 MB).

auth_certificate.description: The X.509 Certificate (PEM encoded) to use for mTLS authentication against the upstream (Docker only). Use the file() function to read this from a file.

auth_certificate_key.description: The Certificate private key (PEM encoded) to use for mTLS authentication against the upstream (Docker only). Use the file() function to read this from a file.

auth_mode.description: The authentication mode to use when accessing this upstream.

auth_secret.description: Secret to provide with requests to upstream.

auth_username.description: Username to provide with requests to upstream.

component.description: (deb only) The component to fetch from the upstream.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the Upstream was created.

distro_version.description: (rpm only) The distribution version that packages found on this upstream will be associated with.

distro_versions.description: (deb only) The distribution versions that packages found on this upstream will be associated with.

extra_header_1.description: The key for extra header #1 to send to upstream.

extra_header_2.description: The key for extra header #2 to send to upstream.

extra_value_1.description: The value for extra header #1 to send to upstream. This is stored as plaintext, and is NOT encrypted.

extra_value_2.description: The value for extra header #2 to send to upstream. This is stored as plaintext, and is NOT encrypted.

include_sources.description: (deb/rpm only) When true, source packages will be available from this upstream.

is_active.description: Whether or not this upstream is active and ready for requests.

mode.description: The mode that this upstream should operate in. Upstream sources can be used to proxy resolved packages, as well as operate in a proxy/cache or cache only mode.

name.description: A descriptive name for this upstream source. A shortened version of this name will be used for tagging cached packages retrieved from this upstream.

namespace.description: The Organization to which the Upstream belongs.

priority.description: Upstream sources are selected for resolving requests by sequential order (1..n), followed by creation date.

repository.description: The Repository to which the Upstream belongs.

slug_perm.description: The unique identifier for this Upstream.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the Upstream was updated.

upstream_distribution.description: (deb only) The distribution to fetch from the upstream.

upstream_prefix.description: (generic only) A unique prefix used to distinguish this upstream source within the repository. Requests including this prefix are routed to this upstream.

upstream_type.description: The type of Upstream (docker, nuget, python, ...)

upstream_url.description: The URL for this upstream source. This must be a fully qualified URL including any path elements required to reach the root of the repository.

verify_ssl.description: If enabled, SSL certificates are verified when requests are made to this upstream. It's recommended to leave this enabled for all public sources to help mitigate Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) attacks. Please note this only applies to HTTPS upstreams.

saml_auth_enabled.description: Enable SAML authentication for the organization

saml_auth_enforced.description: Enforce SAML authentication for the organization

package_query.description: The package-based search query for webhooks to fire. This uses the same syntax as the standard search used for repositories, and also supports boolean logic operators such as OR/AND/NOT and parentheses for grouping. If a package does not match, the webhook will not fire.

repository.description: Repository to which this webhook belongs.

request_body_format.description: The format of the payloads for webhook requests.

request_body_template_format.description: The format of the payloads for webhook requests.

request_content_type.description: The value that will be sent for the 'Content Type' header.

secret_header.description: The header to send the predefined secret in. This must be unique from existing headers or it won't be sent. You can use this as a form of authentication on the endpoint side.

secret_value.description: The value for the predefined secret (note: this is treated as a passphrase and is encrypted when we store it). You can use this as a form of authentication on the endpoint side.

signature_key.description: The value for the signature key - This is used to generate an HMAC-based hex digest of the request body, which we send as the X-Cloudsmith-Signature header so that you can ensure that the request wasn't modified by a malicious party (note: this is treated as a passphrase and is encrypted when we store it).

slug_perm.description: The slug_perm immutably identifies the webhook. It will never change once a webhook has been created.

target_url.description: The destination URL that webhook payloads will be POST'ed to.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the webhook was updated.

updated_by.description: The user/account that updated the webhook.

verify_ssl.description: If enabled, SSL certificates is verified when webhooks are sent. It's recommended to leave this enabled as not verifying the integrity of SSL certificates leaves you susceptible to Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks.

active_token.description: If true, only include active tokens

query.description: A search term for querying names of entitlements.

show_token.description: Show entitlement token strings in results.

npm_upstream_tags_take_precedence.description: If checked, npm distribution tags from configured upstreams will take precedence over matching local tags. When both upstream and local repositories have the same tag name (e.g., 'latest'), the upstream tag will be used instead of the local one, even if the local repository has a semantically higher version.

nuget_native_signing_enabled.description: When enabled, all pushed (or pulled from upstream) nuget packages and artifacts will be signed using the repository's X.509 RSA certificate. Additionally, the nuget RepositorySignature index will list all of the repository's signing certificates including the ones from configured upstreams.

proxy_npmjs.description: If checked, Npm packages that are not in the repository when requested by clients will automatically be proxied from the public npmjs.org registry. If there is at least one version for a package, others will not be proxied.

proxy_pypi.description: If checked, Python packages that are not in the repository when requested by clients will automatically be proxied from the public pypi.python.org registry. If there is at least one version for a package, others will not be proxied.

raw_package_index_enabled.description: If checked, HTML and JSON indexes will be generated that list all available raw packages in the repository.

raw_package_index_signatures_enabled.description: If checked, the HTML and JSON indexes will display raw package GPG signatures alongside the index packages.

replace_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to republish packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific republish setting. Please note that the user still requires the privilege to delete packages that will be replaced by the new package; otherwise the republish will fail.

replace_packages_by_default.description: If checked, uploaded packages will overwrite/replace any others with the same attributes (e.g. same version) by default. This only applies if the user has the required privilege for the republishing AND has the required privilege to delete existing packages that they don't own.

repository_type.description: The repository type changes how it is accessed and billed. Private repositories can only be used on paid plans, but are visible only to you or authorised delegates. Public repositories are free to use on all plans and visible to all Cloudsmith users.

resync_own.description: If checked, users can resync any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

resync_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to resync packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific resync setting.

scan_own.description: If checked, users can scan any of their own packages that they have uploaded, assuming that they still have write privilege for the repository. This takes precedence over privileges configured in the 'Access Controls' section of the repository, and any inherited from the org.

scan_packages.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to scan packages. Unless the package was uploaded by that user, in which the permission may be overridden by the user-specific scan setting.

self_url.description: API endpoint where data about this repository can be retrieved.

show_setup_all.description: If checked, the Set Me Up help for all formats will always be shown, even if you don't have packages of that type uploaded. Otherwise, help will only be shown for packages that are in the repository. For example, if you have uploaded only NuGet packages, then the Set Me Up help for NuGet packages will be shown only.

slug.description: The slug identifies the repository in URIs.

slug_perm.description: The slug_perm immutably identifies the repository. It will never change once a repository has been created.

storage_region.description: The Cloudsmith region in which package files are stored.

strict_npm_validation.description: If checked, npm packages will be validated strictly to ensure the package matches specifcation. You can turn this off if you have packages that are old or otherwise mildly off-spec, but we can't guarantee the packages will work with npm-cli or other tooling correctly. Turn off at your own risk!

tag_pre_releases_as_latest.description: If checked, packages pushed with a pre-release component on that version will be marked with the 'latest' tag. Note that if unchecked, a repository containing ONLY pre-release versions, will have no version marked latest which may cause incompatibility with native tools

use_debian_labels.description: If checked, a 'Label' field will be present in Debian-based repositories. It will contain a string that identifies the entitlement token used to authenticate the repository, in the form of 'source=t-'; or 'source=none' if no token was used. You can use this to help with pinning.

use_default_cargo_upstream.description: If checked, dependencies of uploaded Cargo crates which do not set an explicit value for "registry" will be assumed to be available from crates.io. If unchecked, dependencies with unspecified "registry" values will be assumed to be available in the registry being uploaded to. Uncheck this if you want to ensure that dependencies are only ever installed from Cloudsmith unless explicitly specified as belong to another registry.

use_entitlements_privilege.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to see/use entitlement tokens with private repositories. If a user does not have the permission, they will only be able to download packages using other credentials, such as email/password via basic authentication. Use this if you want to force users to only use their user-based token, which is tied to their access (if removed, they can't use it). Possible values: Read, Write, Admin.

use_noarch_packages.description: If checked, noarch packages (if supported) are enabled in installations/configurations. A noarch package is one that is not tied to specific system architecture (like i686).

use_source_packages.description: If checked, source packages (if supported) are enabled in installations/configurations. A source package is one that contains source code rather than built binaries.

use_vulnerability_scanning.description: If checked, vulnerability scanning will be enabled for all supported packages within this repository.

user_entitlements_enabled.description: If checked, users can use and manage their own user-specific entitlement token for the repository (if private). Otherwise, user-specific entitlements are disabled for all users.

view_statistics.description: This defines the minimum level of privilege required for a user to view repository statistics, to include entitlement-based usage, if applicable. If a user does not have the permission, they won't be able to view any statistics, either via the UI, API or CLI.

namespace.description: Organization to which the source Repository belongs.

repository.description: Source Repository whose connected repositories are listed.

organization.description: Organization to which this repository belongs.
Organization to which the service belongs.

service.description: Slug of the service to retrieve.

organization.description: Organization within which to list service accounts.
Organization within which to list teams.
Organization to which this team belongs.

team_name.description: Name (slug) of the team whose members to list.

slug_perm.description: The slug_perm immutably identifies the user
